title: Threshold correlation and absolute mean
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $p$ be a real coefficient family indexed by subsets of $\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, and let $f$ be a real-valued function on the Boolean cube. If $f(x)$ equals $1$ when the polynomial represented by $p$ is nonnegative at $x$, and equals $-1$ otherwise, then the uniform expectation of the absolute value of that polynomial equals its uniform inner product with $f$.
hypotheses_covered: $p$ is a real coefficient family on subsets of the coordinate set
$f$ is a real-valued function on the Boolean cube
$f$ equals the threshold sign of the polynomial represented by $p$
replaced: Let $n\ge0$ and equip $\{0,1\}^n$ with its uniform probability measure; write $\mathbb E$ for uniform expectation. For $S\subseteq[n]$, put $\chi_S(x)=\prod_{i\in S}(-1)^{x_i}$ and $\widehat h(S)=\mathbb E[h\chi_S]$ for real cube functions $h$. Let $P(x)=\sum_{S\subseteq[n]}a_S\chi_S(x)$ with real coefficients $a_S$. If $f(x)=1$ when $P(x)\ge0$ and $f(x)=-1$ when $P(x)<0$, then $\mathbb E|P|=\mathbb E[Pf]$.
